name: Optimization

subjectOf.text: The regulatory sine curve itself may be inevitable, but its costly and suboptimal regulatory effects can nonetheless be limited.
subjectOf.abstract: While the sine curve may be inevitable, its costly and suboptimal regulatory effects can be limited.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Dynamic Regulation of the Financial Services Industry (2013). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=2273857

subjectOf.text: Business and regulatory cycles will persist, but optimizing the relationship between indicators of financial crises and the regulatory sine curve, especially the timing of regulatory responses, could soften some of the effects of crises.
subjectOf.abstract: While business and regulatory cycles are bound to persist, optimizing the relationship between indicators for financial crises and the regulatory sine curve, especially the timing of regulatory responses to crises, could soften some of the effects of regulatory crises.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Dynamic Regulation of the Financial Services Industry (2013). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=2273857
scope_conditions: cycles themselves are taken as given

subjectOf.text: Where human managers satisfice because further search is cognitively costly, AI2AI agents continue searching until the global optimum is reached, because additional computation is essentially free.
subjectOf.abstract: Where human managers satisfice because further search is cognitively costly, AI2AI agents continue searching until the global optimum is reached—because additional computation is essentially free.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, The AI-to-AI Economy and the Collapse of Anthropocentric Economic Theory (2025). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=5886442
scope_conditions: assumes compute is cheap relative to the value of further search

subjectOf.text: Human managers satisfice because further search is cognitively costly, whereas AI agents continue searching until the global optimum is reached because additional computation is essentially free, which removes bounded rationality from the economic substrate.
subjectOf.abstract: Where human managers satisfice because further search is cognitively costly, AI2AI agents continue searching until the global optimum is reached because additional computation is essentially free.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, The Collapse of Scarcity Economics (2026). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=6421319
scope_conditions: applies to autonomous agents with effectively unbounded computational capacity
